I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best and can manage steadily at my age: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the land for the full year, match the local water and weather, and avoid taking on crops that need more labor, market risk, or complicated management. I will stay with familiar field crops instead of cotton, vegetables, or something new, because I want reliable grain, simpler fieldwork, and work that fits what I already know. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for disease, aphids, and weeds. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize right away for better yield, use a bit more nitrogen, irrigate only when necessary, and control weeds and insects with a few timely applications. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing, and it is the practical choice for moving quickly between wheat and maize in one year.
